reason: Takizuka–Abe binary pairing approximates the Fokker–Planck operator only in aggregate. Langevin collision operators are a separate Monte Carlo scheme, not equivalent.

fix.summary: Coulomb collisions act as Fokker–Planck diffusion and drag in velocity space. In PIC codes this is done by Monte Carlo: either binary-collision pairing (Takizuka–Abe), which reproduces the Fokker–Planck operator on average, or Langevin (stochastic-differential-equation) kicks.

reason: The map is just Gauss's law, which is filler. It should name the PIC structure.

fix.map: macroparticles pushed by Lorentz force ↔ fields on a Yee grid (FDTD Maxwell), charge/current deposited back to the grid

reason: Godunov/Riemann solvers came from gas dynamics and were extended to MHD. Only constrained transport (Evans–Hawley 1988) was developed for MHD.

fix.summary: Numerical MHD has to keep ∇·B=0. Constrained transport (Evans–Hawley 1988, staggered fluxes) or divergence cleaning (projection, hyperbolic GLM) does this, combined with Godunov-type Riemann solvers that were extended from gas dynamics to the MHD wave system. These are now standard in astrophysical MHD codes.

reason: Filler: the clause about astrophysical turbulence reviews adds nothing.

fix.summary: Pseudo-spectral direct numerical simulation of the incompressible and reduced MHD Elsasser equations is the main test of anisotropic cascade and critical-balance predictions. Finite resolution limits the inertial range and Reynolds number, so spectral-index measurements (−5/3 vs −3/2) remain uncertain.

reason: The Boris scheme is volume-preserving but not symplectic (Qin et al. 2013). It is a standard plasma tool rather than structural in numerical analysis.

fix.summary: The Boris algorithm advances charged particles in E and B with a half-electric/rotation/half-electric split. It is time-reversible and volume-preserving but not symplectic (Qin et al. 2013), which explains its bounded long-term energy error. It is the default PIC pusher and a precursor of explicitly symplectic and structure-preserving schemes.

reason: Not an identity. Kramers–Kronig fails for unstable plasmas (poles in the upper half-plane), and the conductor pole at ω=0 needs subtraction.

fix.summary: Causality makes the plasma dielectric ε(k,ω) at fixed k analytic in the upper half ω-plane for stable equilibria. Kramers–Kronig relations then link the reactive part to the dissipative (Landau-damping) part.
fix.breaks: Fails for unstable distributions, whose response has upper-half-plane poles. The free-carrier pole at ω=0 must be subtracted. Spatial dispersion means the relations hold at fixed k only.

reason: The DSA power law follows from a simple steady advection–diffusion flux balance. There is no substantive complex-analysis or special-function link, and the summary cites a 'shared paper' as filler.
duplicate of C0413 (self-adjoint MHD force operator, energy principle); merged there
This is a method transfer, not an identity. Real ω² holds only for static equilibria. Absorbs the energy principle from C0411.

fix.summary: For static equilibria the linear ideal-MHD force operator F is self-adjoint under the kinetic-energy inner product. Spectral theory therefore gives real ω², a Rayleigh–Ritz energy principle δW (Bernstein et al. 1958) and a spectrum with discrete modes plus Alfvén and slow continua. With equilibrium flows, the Frieman–Rotenberg operator is non-self-adjoint in this sense, and stability is no longer decided by δW alone.
fix.breaks: Static equilibria only; flows make the problem non-normal.

reason: This is a spectral-theory method (generalized eigenfunctions in a rigged Hilbert space), not a shared mechanism. The map omits the van Kampen eigenfunction form.

fix.map: van Kampen mode δf_v ∝ P[1/(ω−kv)]·∂_v f_0 + λ(ω)δ(ω−kv) ↔ generalized eigenvectors of a continuous spectrum

reason: The frozen-in flux theorem belongs to ideal MHD rather than dynamo theory.

fix.summary: Given ∇·B=0, the ideal induction equation is exactly Lie transport of the magnetic flux 2-form, which yields Alfvén's frozen-in theorem and the Cauchy solution. Magnetic helicity ∫A∧dA is a topological (linking) invariant of this transport.

reason: Interferometry and Thomson scattering do not rely on sheath physics. Debye length enters Thomson scattering through the Salpeter parameter.

fix.summary: Langmuir-probe I–V curves give T_e from the exponential electron-retardation region and n_e from the ion saturation current via sheath theory and the Bohm criterion, which assumes λ_D much smaller than the probe size. In Thomson scattering, kλ_D (the Salpeter parameter) separates the incoherent regime (giving T_e) from the collective regime.

reason: Not an identity. Quasi-symmetry gives a conserved momentum only for guiding-centre motion at leading order, and exact global QS is believed impossible (Garren–Boozer).

fix.breaks: Holds only for guiding-centre dynamics at leading order in ρ*. Garren–Boozer argue that exact quasi-symmetry cannot hold throughout a volume, so real devices are only approximately quasi-symmetric.

reason: This is Noether applied to an ignorable angle, so a shared mechanism rather than an identity. Toroidal-field ripple breaks it.

fix.breaks: Exact only for exact axisymmetry. Toroidal-field ripple and 3D perturbations break p_φ conservation, causing ripple losses.

reason: Cross-helicity follows from relabelling symmetry (Padhye–Morrison 1996). Magnetic helicity is a Casimir/topological invariant, not a plain Noether charge. Kind and strength are overstated.

fix.summary: In ideal MHD, cross-helicity is the Noether charge of fluid-element relabelling symmetry (Padhye–Morrison 1996). Magnetic helicity ∫A·B dV is a Casimir and linking-number invariant. Together they constrain Taylor relaxation, dynamo α-quenching and inverse cascades.
fix.breaks: Magnetic helicity is not straightforwardly the Noether charge of a physical symmetry; its derivation through gauge or relabelling arguments is still being debated.

reason: Adiabatic invariants are asymptotic (Kruskal), not exact conservation laws. They break under resonances or when ρ/L is not small, so this is not an identity.

fix.breaks: Asymptotic only: conserved to all orders in ρ/L, but destroyed by resonances, chaotic orbits (Chirikov overlap) or fast field variation.

reason: The α-effect needs explicitly, not spontaneously, broken mirror symmetry. The order parameter is field amplitude, not growth rate.

fix.summary: Dynamo onset is a bifurcation in which the saturated field picks a sign, spontaneously breaking the B→−B symmetry of the induction equation. Geodynamo reversals are then transitions between the ± states (Pétrélis–Fauve). Separately, the α-effect requires explicitly broken mirror symmetry (kinetic helicity) of the flow.
fix.map: field amplitude |B| ↔ order parameter; B→−B ↔ Z₂ symmetry

reason: Anderson (1963) treated the superconductor's Goldstone phase mode, not a phonon, being lifted to the plasma frequency by Coulomb coupling.

fix.summary: Anderson (1963) showed that the Coulomb interaction lifts the superconductor's gapless Goldstone phase mode to the plasma frequency. He noted that a plasma likewise gives the photon an effective mass ω_p. This was a prototype of the Higgs mechanism.

reason: A specific application in plasma, but not structural on the dimensional-analysis side. Connor–Taylor scale invariance should be credited.

fix.summary: Kadomtsev's constraint and Connor–Taylor scale invariance reduce tokamak confinement to dimensionless ρ*, β, ν*, q and shape. Gyro-Bohm transport χ ~ ρ*·T/eB is the ρ*-scaling used to extrapolate confinement to ITER.

reason: The plasmoid S-independent rate is mainly a numerical result. The link is an application on the dimensional-analysis side.

fix.summary: Mass and flux balance give the Sweet–Parker inflow rate v_in/V_A ~ S^{-1/2}. Simulations show that above S_c ~ 10^4 the current sheet goes plasmoid-unstable and the rate saturates near 0.01 V_A, roughly independent of S.

reason: The MHD spectral index is still contested (Boldyrev's −3/2 vs Goldreich–Sridhar −5/3). Iroshnikov–Kraichnan gives −3/2, not the mapped −5/3.

fix.summary: Constant-flux dimensional arguments extend Kolmogorov scaling to MHD: Iroshnikov–Kraichnan gives E ∝ k^{-3/2}, while Goldreich–Sridhar critical balance gives E ∝ k_⊥^{-5/3} with k_∥ ∝ k_⊥^{2/3}. Dynamic alignment (Boldyrev) argues for −3/2, so the index remains contested.

reason: Broad application, not structural in both fields. The similarity claim should name the Ryutov scaling.

fix.summary: Plasma regimes are classified by dimensionless groups: the plasma parameter nλ_D³, Lundquist number, β, ρ* and collisionality. Ryutov-type Euler similarity (1999) uses invariance of ideal MHD to scale laser-plasma experiments to astrophysical flows.

reason: Too vague, and strength is overstated. Structure prediction is not a physics surrogate. It should name AlphaFold2 and equivariant interatomic potentials.

fix.summary: Deep networks (AlphaFold2, 2021) predict protein structure from sequence and coevolution without integrating physical dynamics. Separately, equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials, trained on quantum-chemistry data, replace force fields in biomolecular MD.

reason: Vague. It should name how MD yields transport coefficients.

fix.summary: MD, including with machine-learned potentials, computes ionic diffusion and conductivity in solid electrolytes and battery materials. It uses mean-square displacement or Green–Kubo current autocorrelations, with Nernst–Einstein relations and Haven ratios to account for correlated hopping.

reason: Absorbs C0433: folding drove MD development, and MD trajectories test energy-landscape theory.

fix.summary: Force-field MD, enhanced sampling (replica exchange, metadynamics) and special-purpose hardware (Anton; Lindorff-Larsen et al. 2011, fast-folding proteins) simulate folding, binding and conformational change. Folding timescales drove these MD advances, and the atomistic trajectories test funnel energy-landscape theory.

reason: duplicate of C0432
Dose calculation uses analog transport Monte Carlo with condensed history, not Metropolis Markov-chain sampling. Strength is overstated on the Monte Carlo node's side.

fix.summary: Monte Carlo radiation transport (EGSnrc, Geant4/TOPAS) samples individual particle histories, using condensed-history electron transport. It is the gold standard for dose calculation in photon and proton therapy and the benchmark for fast analytic algorithms.

reason: Dynamic-aperture tracking typically runs 10^5–10^7 turns, not billions.

fix.summary: Long-term tracking in storage rings uses symplectic maps and integrators so that dynamic-aperture studies over 10^5–10^7 turns have no artificial damping or growth, as in long-term celestial mechanics.

reason: Fourier transforms belong to the differential-equations/transforms node. The MRI signal is a Fourier transform only after neglecting relaxation and off-resonance, so this is not an identity.

fix.summary: With relaxation, off-resonance and coil sensitivity neglected, the MRI signal samples the Fourier transform of the magnetisation along gradient-defined k-space trajectories. In CT, the Fourier slice theorem maps each projection's 1D transform to a line through the object's 2D transform.
fix.breaks: T2* decay, off-resonance and coil profiles make the MRI encoding only approximately Fourier.

reason: This is a method transfer, not a shared physical mechanism.
Narrowed to avoid overlap with C0443 (Fourier slice). Not structural on the linear-algebra side.

fix.summary: Tomographic reconstruction is an ill-posed linear inverse problem g = Af. SVD shows how small singular values amplify noise, and Tikhonov or total-variation regularisation and iterative solvers (ART, OSEM) stabilise it, beyond filtered back-projection.

reason: Gauss–Bonnet makes the Gaussian-curvature term a topological constant. It affects topology changes, not shape at fixed topology.

fix.summary: Membranes are treated as 2D surfaces whose mean curvature H and Gaussian curvature K enter the Helfrich energy. By Gauss–Bonnet, ∫K dA = 2πχ, so the κ̄ term is constant at fixed topology and matters only for fusion, fission and pore formation.

reason: Vague and partly misattributed. SQUIDs are limited by Johnson and 1/f noise; spin sensors by photon shot noise and spin-projection noise.

fix.summary: Quantum sensors inherit instrumentation noise floors and modulation techniques. SQUIDs are limited by Johnson noise in their shunts and by 1/f flux noise. NV and atomic magnetometers are limited by photon shot noise and spin-projection noise (the standard quantum limit). They use lock-in demodulation, e.g. frequency-modulated ODMR, to avoid 1/f noise.

reason: Molecular point groups are finite groups, not Lie groups, so the subfield node fits better. This is applied representation theory, a method transfer.
Not a Noether link. The Courant–Snyder invariant is the action of linear Hill-equation motion, and emittance follows from Liouville. This belongs to Hamiltonian mechanics ↔ beam dynamics.
Overclaim: Goldstone-like soft modes do exist out of equilibrium (Toner–Tu flocks, phase diffusion of Turing patterns).

fix.breaks: Patterns arise from non-equilibrium bifurcations in finite, driven systems. Soft modes can exist (pattern phase diffusion, Toner–Tu), but no equilibrium Goldstone or Mermin–Wagner theorem governs them.

reason: Too generic. Named the specific scalings.

fix.summary: Scaling sets cell-scale physics. Swimming bacteria have Re ~ 10^-4, so inertia is irrelevant and reciprocal strokes fail (Purcell's scallop theorem). The membrane length √(κ/σ), tens to hundreds of nm, separates bending-dominated from tension-dominated regimes and sets tether radii.

reason: Josephson and quantum Hall standards are condensed-matter standards rather than quantum sensors. The link to quantum sensing runs through atom-based SI realisations.

fix.summary: Atom-based quantum sensors realise or test SI units directly from atomic invariants. Cs and optical clocks realise the second, atom-interferometric h/m measurements give α, and Rydberg-atom electrometry gives SI-traceable electric fields through atomic dipole moments.
fix.map: E = ħΩ_R/d (Rydberg Rabi frequency), Δν_Cs fixed

record.name: δf particle methods as control-variate variance reduction
record.summary: Gyrokinetic PIC codes evolve only the perturbation δf = f − f_0 with weighted markers. This is the control-variate variance-reduction technique of Monte Carlo integration, cutting sampling noise by roughly (δf/f)² compared with full-f.
record.map: ∫A f dv = ∫A f_0 dv (analytic) + Σ_i w_i A(z_i), w_i = δf/g at markers

record.name: PIC grid resolution of the Debye length
record.summary: Explicit momentum-conserving PIC needs grid spacing comparable to λ_D, or aliasing drives the finite-grid instability and numerical heating. It also needs ω_pΔt ≲ 2 for stability. Energy-conserving and implicit schemes relax these limits.

record.name: Reinforcement-learned magnetic control and disruption prediction
record.summary: Deep reinforcement learning has controlled TCV tokamak plasma shapes directly through the coil voltages (Degrave et al. 2022). Neural disruption predictors trained across machines give real-time warnings. Transfer to ITER-class devices is still unproven.
record.map: policy π(coil voltages | magnetic measurements) ↔ feedback shape controller
